what: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, holds bitcoin as its main asset. It issues shares and fixed-income securities and uses the proceeds to buy more bitcoin, and it still sells the enterprise analytics software the company was originally built on.
customers: Enterprise software customers for the analytics products; investors are the real audience for the bitcoin strategy.
money: enterprise analytics licences and cloud subscriptions
bitcoin bought with money raised in capital markets
moat: No conventional moat: the software business is small and anyone can buy bitcoin. Its real advantage is the ability to raise capital at a scale no other bitcoin holder has.
risks: The shares move with bitcoin, amplified by borrowed money in both directions
Large reported losses come from writing bitcoin down when its price falls
Debt of about $7 billion plus preferred dividends must be serviced whatever bitcoin does
If the shares fall below the value of the bitcoin per share, issuing new shares destroys value
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, though the estimate is really a view on bitcoin
Issuing shares above the value of bitcoin per share raises bitcoin per share
It holds far more bitcoin than any other listed company
watch: Bitcoin per share, total debt and preferred obligations, and the premium to the value of its holdings.
